findings.reason: adding the informing edge the prose already asserts would let a coordinator schedule and close both halves together, instead of reading §5 as repairing the read-only worktree on its own when the plan itself says the release half lives in the other plan.
findings.text: §5 states that `a-queued-request-is-checked-when-queued` §5 "is the companion that stops the release", but the plan declares only `plan-depends-on: a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner` and no `plan-informs` (or section relationship) to that plan, which is still `active` — so the single mechanism §5 describes is split across two plans that the roadmap shows as unrelated

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the §16 anchors resolve at the base (paired dispatch creating both run directories at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1353`, `claim_published = not shadow_lineage` at `:2578`, `_supervisor_write` at `:2774`, `record_reservation_supervisor` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2495` under `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` at `:2515`, `held_launch_reservation`'s bare presence check at `:2417`, `skip_ended` at `:2396`/`:3521`, the retired-receipt strict read at `:2159`, the vacuous `assert pid > 0` at `tests/test_a_concurrent_launch_is_refused.py:446` and `:461`, and `test_a_fresh_run_id_takes_no_reservation` at `:776`), and the two cited evidence files exist with the anchored ids they are linked by.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every section states a measurable done-when; the open §16 declares logged mutations with FAILED ids and a non-zero EXIT per behaviour change, and §17 declares `none` with the reason that it deletes code no production path reaches.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs and evidence sit under the run directory and under `docs/evidence/`, both durable; §14's only output is `docs/evidence/fragments/a-run-has-one-live-worker/find-the-second-launcher-of-a-figure-finding.html`, which exists.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the symbols and test filenames the remaining section introduces (`launch_reservation_key`, `run_holds_an_attempt_record`, `held_launch_reservation`, `test_a_fresh_run_ids_reservation_ends_with_its_launch`) name the mechanism, and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose is carried into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold for the open section: its six root causes match the code I read (paired directory pre-creation, the shadow-skipped claim publication, the `suppress(OSError)` around the supervisor rewrite, and the two vacuous test assertions), its mechanism produces its done-when (`run_holds_an_attempt_record` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2286` does count `attempt.json`, which is what makes the marker-before-key ordering and the attempt-1 resume case reachable), and it names the callers on the real code path (`dispatch.py:2863` dispatch door, `dispatch_launch.py:3076` in `supervised_launch`, `:3517` the spawn guard, `:2457` `reserve_launch_attempt` for the admit door).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16's three behaviour changes are one deliverable, "the launch reservation leaves no stray state", and the two test-defect repairs it absorbs are the measurement of that same mechanism.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 names `a-queued-request-is-checked-when-queued` §5 as the companion that stops the worktree release, and the plan declares no relationship to it.
